text:
alex: quick Q — I noticed a terraform change in the shared-k8s-module that removed the annotations block from the ServiceAccount resource. It broke our payments pod who relied on IRSA. Is it safe to re-add the eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn annotation at module level?
leah: whoa — which module change? link?
alex: https://git/repo/infra/commit/8f3b — the sa template used to have annotations: { eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn = var.sa_role_arn } and now it's gone. The deployment helm chart expects the SA to carry the annotation for IRSA mapping.
juan: FYI we generally prefer terraform to own the SA annotation only if TF is creating the SA. If helm creates the SA (helm chart has `createServiceAccount: true`) then helm needs the annotation. Mixing ownership causes drift.
alex: in our case TF creates the SA in the module, and the chart references that SA by name (createServiceAccount: false). So TF should be authoritative.
leah: ok then re-adding is fine, but two gotchas: 1) ensure the role ARN value is provided per-environment (TF var). 2) if you use a namespace label gating (like `infra/managed: "true"`) the module should only add annotations when label present, otherwise we accidentally annotate 3rd-party namespaces.
alex: good call. The change removed annotations to avoid unwanted annotations in tenant namespaces. We added a label check in the new module API but forgot to wire it for the role_arn case.
sam: small suggestion: instead of hard annotation, we can attach the IRSA mapping via aws_iam_role_policy_attachment + OIDC provider and use `eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn` on SA — that's still annotation-based. There's no separate binding mechanism at k8s level.
juan: also check automountServiceAccountToken: if pods have that disabled, projected tokens won't mount even with the annotation.
ale x: (typo) alex: good point — payments deployment has automountServiceAccountToken: true.
infra-bot: deploy status: staging/payments v2.4.1 FAILED — SA denied access to S3 bucket (403).
leah: to debug, run:
```
kubectl -n payments get sa payments-sa -o yaml
kubectl -n payments describe pod <failed-pod>
kubectl -n payments exec -it <pod> -- cat /var/run/secrets/eks.amazonaws.com/serviceaccount/token
```
juan: if token exists, check that the token has `aud` and `sub` matching the IAM trust policy — recently we rotated OIDC provider; trust policy expects `system:serviceaccount:payments:payments-sa`. If namespace changed or SA name mismatch, role won't assume.
alex: I ran get sa and the annotation was missing in staging, but present in prod. So the module change hit staging. I can open a quick PR to re-add annotation behind the namespace label check.
leah: please also add a migration note in the module README and a terraform plan guard to catch removing annotations accidentally.
sam: for extra safety, add a test in CI that checks service accounts that are expected to be IRSA-bound have the annotation after apply (kubectl diff or k8s provider read).
juan: one more edge: if you're using `kubernetes_manifest` or `helm_release` with `atomic: true` the order can flip — ensure SA is created before pods. Use `depends_on` in TF or helm hooks.
alex: thanks — I'll push the PR with the annotation reintroduce + label gating + a short CI check. Ping me if anyone wants to review.
leah: pinged alex for review when ready :thumbsup:
infra-bot: ci/terraform plan passed for branch alex/readd-irsa-annotation (staging)
